data.cultural_impact: The name Anbarasan is deeply rooted in the cultural traditions of Tamil Nadu, a region in southern India that is known for its rich heritage and deep spirituality. Lord Murugan, who is also known as Kartikeya and Shanmukha, is considered the god of war and fertility. The name Anbarasan evokes a sense of strength and power, as well as deep compassion and mercy. In Hindu mythology, Lord Murugan is depicted as the commander-in-chief of the army of gods, and he is also considered the god of love and compassion.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Anbarasan has deep spiritual significance in Hinduism. The name reflects the divine qualities of mercy and compassion, which are intrinsic to Lord Murugan. Anbarasan is believed to bestow his blessings on his devotees, bringing peace, happiness, and prosperity into their lives. The name also symbolizes the power of mercy and compassion to overcome hardships and challenges. In Hindu mythology, Lord Murugan is often depicted as holding a spear in his hand, symbolizing the power to vanquish evil, and a bowl of fruit, symbolizing the power to bestow blessings upon his devotees. The name Anbarasan serves as a constant reminder of the power of mercy and compassion in the face of adversity and hardship.

historical_references.reference: Anbarasan was a Chola general during the reign of Rajaraja Chola I (985-1014 CE). He is famous for his victory over the Chalukya king, Taila II, in the Battle of Tambaram (1013 CE).

Anbarasan was a devotee of Lord Murugan and is known for his role in the story of 'Anbarasan and Avvaiyar'. According to the legend, Avvaiyar, an ancient Tamil poetess, was angry with Lord Murugan for not granting her the boon of immortality. Anbarasan, who was in love with Avvaiyar, went to Lord Murugan and asked for her immortality instead. Impressed by Anbarasan's selflessness, Lord Murugan granted Avvaiyar the boon of immortality.
